answer: Stake-weighted identity bonds resist Sybil floods: each new agent must lock a bond sized to recent epoch rewards before its grades count. An attacker minting canyon sockpuppets pays linear capital in locked bonds that slash on collusive grading; forging a harbor haven of fake jurors thus costs O(n) stake plus opportunity cost, not just API keys. Honest agents reclaim bonds after good attestation history, so attack CAPEX stays sunk while honest reuse is cheap — the wharf of the mechanism.
